I’m 76 now, and my back aches when the weather turns. It’s just me and my wife at home, so I can’t run around like I did thirty years ago. But I’ve farmed these fields in Quzhou for half a century, and I know every lump of soil. I have 8 mu and a well for irrigation. I grow cotton, maize, and wheat, but the backbone of my farm is the wheat-maize rotation. It gives me grain to eat and sell, and with the machines these days I can manage it without killing myself.

This year I will put 6 mu into the wheat-maize double crop and keep 2 mu for cotton. I won’t expand the cotton because picking it and spraying for bollworms is backbreaking work for an old man, but 2 mu gives me a little cash income without exhausting us.

For the winter wheat on those 6 mu, I will rotary till before sowing in October. I trust the improved wheat seeds I’ve used for years—they give steady yields around 1000 jin per mu if the weather behaves. I will apply about 16 kg of nitrogen, 7 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium per mu. That’s what this soil needs after decades of me working it. I’ll irrigate three times from the well: the revival water in spring, the jointing water, and the grain-filling water. Two pesticide sprays should be enough—one for weeds early on, and one for insects around heading.

For the summer maize on the same 6 mu, I will plant hybrid seed right after the wheat harvest in June. I won’t till the land—there’s barely a week between harvest and planting, and at my age I can’t rush around ploughing in the heat. No-tillage maize grows fine here if you irrigate it properly. I’ll use about 16 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. Maize needs less water than wheat in this season, so two good irrigations will do: one at the big trumpet stage and one during grain filling. Two sprays—herbicide at the start and insecticide later—will protect it. I expect around 1000 jin per mu.

For the 2 mu of cotton, I will plough the soil deeply in spring because cotton roots like loose ground. I’ll sow improved cotton seeds. Fertilizer will be 14 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 7 kg potassium per mu. Cotton is thirsty and buggy, so I’ll irrigate three times—seedling, flowering, and boll stage—and spray four times for aphids and bollworms. If the season is fair, I should harvest about 500 jin of seed cotton per mu.

I don’t chase new tricks anymore. I use what my well, my experience, and my two old hands can reliably manage.
